contract.words: Collect $40,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $40,000 of settled cash received within 30 days with no owner capital advanced

strategy.title: No plan: the monument-dealer list market is capped below the target
strategy.why: 140 dealers in the directory, each buying at most one list package a season, at the established $149 price: even if every dealer bought, settled cash is at most $20,860, against a $40,000 target. At the measured 12-of-60 (20%) conversion the realistic figure is about 28 sales, $4,172.

alternatives.title: Sell the season list package to all 140 dealers
alternatives.why: Rejected as a plan for this target: its whole market tops out at $20,860; it is a plan only under a target of $20,860 or less.

steps.label: Search for further openings (other buyer populations or repeat offers) outside the counted monument-dealer market

sources.claim: 140 monument dealers listed in the state association directory; each buys at most one list package a season
Two lead-list services sell the package at $149

noPlan.decisiveGap: MARKET_VOLUME: 140 counted dealers x one purchase a season x $149 = $20,860 at most, so 269 sales would be needed against 140 possible; the $40,000 target cannot be reached from this opening at any conversion rate.
noPlan.resolution: Lower the target to at most $20,860 (about $4,172 at the measured 20% conversion) and run the list package to the 140 dealers, or research additional buyer populations/openings outside this counted market before re-planning $40,000.

constraints.suggestion: Lower the target to $20,860 or less (the whole counted market at $149); about $4,172 is what the measured 20% conversion supports.

brain.summary: INFEASIBLE AS STATED: the openings held sell into markets research counted whole: every buyer in them agreeing at the top price brings at most $20,860, so they cannot reach the $40,000 still needed. To make it supportable, target: lower the target to about $20,860, the most the openings held bring with every buyer agreeing at the top price. The conclusion covers the openings held; markets nobody has counted are not ruled out, so Brain keeps searching for openings outside them.

card.payer: Owners of monument and memorial dealers
card.reachableChannel: Email to the dealers listed in the state monument builders association's directory
card.offerScope: A season list package, compiled by Brain from public death records and cemetery permits. Paid by card; payout 3 days later.

links.basis: reach: Email to the dealers listed in the state monument builders association's directo
measured on this offer's own sales: 12 accepted of 60 contacts
141 deal(s) needed but only 140 in the window (140 reachable buyers are stated and no repeat purchase is, so one purchase each)
3 days to usable cash against 30 left

facts.value: 140 monument dealers are listed in the state monument builders association's directory; each buys at most one list package a season.
Sell A season list package, compiled by Brain from public death records and cemetery permits. Paid by card; payout 3 days later. to each buyer.
Owners of monument and memorial dealers
Two lead-list services sell a monument-dealer final-date lettering list package at $149 (listing pages, 2026-11).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right and names the decisive gap the evidence decides: MARKET_VOLUME. The card's EVIDENCE buyerVolume counts the whole market (140 dealers in the state association directory, at most one package per season, so at most one each in 30 days). Recomputed: 140 x $149 = $20,860 < $40,000; reaching $40,000 at $149 needs 269 sales against 140 possible. This is a true constraint, not missing evidence: even every dealer buying cannot fit the target. To reach $40,000 from 140 single purchases the price would have to be >= $286, and no record shows any buyer paying more than $149. At the measured 20% conversion (12/60) the realistic figure is ~28 sales, $4,172. Brain's own planner agrees (NOT_VIABLE, ceiling $20,860). The revision correctly proposes no execution and points to research outside the counted market or a target <= $20,860.
findings: Price evidence is two lead-list services' listing price ($149), i.e. a benchmark of what others charge, not a recorded purchase by these buyers; the 12/60 paid orders do not state their price. It does not change the verdict (a price over $286 would be required and nothing supports it), but any later plan on this opening must establish the price paid by these dealers.
No steps spend money, ledger empty, owner capital $0: consistent with the $0 exposure cap.
Constraint suggestion (target <= $20,860) is honest, and the alternative of new buyer populations is correctly left as research rather than counted.
